messages:
Maya: Kicking off a small experiment — trying a lease-band based token throttle + kernel warm-start bias to reduce cold-KV/batch kernel switch penalties. Main idea: keep a small "warm" admit lane that prefers kernels we've recently used and a wider "cold" lane that gets soft-429'd earlier.

Maya: Quick notes from profiling: when we switch from fast int8 kernel -> fallback wavkernel for long seqs, median kernel-switch overhead ~= 3.8ms and p99 ~= 18ms on gtx-pool during microburst. KV miss penalty (first token) adds ~25ms which compounds.

Sam: Can you paste the profiling snippet? also which metrics you want to monitor for success?

Maya: sure — pasted below. Primary success: p95/p99 end-to-end latency + reduction in tail kernel switch counts; secondary: %requests soft-429'd (we want to avoid large #), and KV warm-hit rate.

Maya: ```
# sample trace (shortened)
req_id=abc123 kernel=fast-int8 -> wavkernel switch at token 12 delta=3.9ms
kv_fetch miss=true first_token_delta=24.7ms
batch_size=6 seq_len=1024
end_to_end=132.4ms p99_component=kernel_switch(18.1ms)
```

Leo: OK. Lease-band approach sounds promising. I suggest two concrete levers: (1) lease_band_size = N tokens reserved for warm-lane (prefer same kernel + pinned KV shards); (2) soft_throttle_curve: probability to soft-429 as function of queue_depth and cold_kernel_count.

Natalie: note: KV warmups are skewed by certain tenant patterns — a few heavy users with 90k sequence prefixes cause many misses. Maybe combine with tenant-cohorting so warm-lane favors recently-seen tenant shards.

Jay: For the soft-429 curve, recommend target p95 increase <= 5% relative to baseline under similar throughput. And cap soft-429 rate to <3% in steady state. Otherwise we risk user-visible regressions.

Maya: Good constraints. Proposed experiment plan: roll canary to 10% traffic on canary pool with settings: lease_band_tokens=64, warm_kernel_bias=true, soft_429_slope=0.18, tenant_cohorting=enabled. Collect: kernel_switch_count, kv_hit_rate_by_tenant, p50/95/99 latency, soft_429_rate.

Sam: Small nit: 64 tokens might be too big for microbatch (<4 tokens per request typical). Maybe express lease_band as % of avg_request_tokens or adaptive min(max(4, 0.1*avg_tokens), 64).

Maya: Good point — will use adaptive formula in rollout config.

infra-bot: deploybot: canary deployment started for service=runtime-pool-7 config=leaseband-v1 target=10%

Leo: Also instrument kernel-affinity metric: fraction of batches where kernel stayed same across sequences; we should see affinity go up in the warm lane. If affinity doesn't increase, lease band isn't capturing locality.

Natalie: Will add KV per-shard heatmap to Grafana so we can see if warm-lane picks hot shards. I expect initial jump in kv_hit_rate for canary traffic.

Maya: If we see too many soft-429s early, fallback plan: reduce soft_429_slope by 40% and increase warm-band size slightly, and enable gradual admission (probabilistic immediate admit ramp over 30s).

Jay: Add a rollback SLA: if p99 increases >25ms or error rate increases >0.3% for 5m, auto-roll back.

Sam: Logging proposal for the thread: add lightweight counters to each admission decision: reason={warm, cold, kernel_mismatch, tenant_heavy} and include short sample of dropped request id in metrics for postmortem (no PII).

Maya: Action items:
- Maya: push canary config with adaptive leaseband and metrics (in 30m)
- Natalie: add KV shard heatmap and tenant cohort tag to metrics (EOD)
- Leo: add kernel-affinity gauge and admission reason counters (today)
- Sam: review sampling & privacy for dropped req ids (today)
- Jay: set rollback SLA and soft-429 cap in deploy (before canary)

Maya: Anyone want to add constraints or foresee risk vectors?

Leo: risk — oscillation if warm-band too small + aggressive soft-429; add damping (no more than 10% band change per minute).

Natalie: watch billing delta for KV egress during canary; warmups may temporarily increase seq token cost.

Maya: thanks — will start. updating thread with canary URL and dashboard links once live. :rocket:
